content:
Today marks nine months since the Wang Fuk Court fire. The Tin Hau Temple at Yuen Chau Tsai, adjacent to Tai Po's Wang Fuk Court, held a ritual this morning in accordance with Hoklo (Hailufeng) tradition to honour the deceased, and specially prepared 200 dedication bags for the victims of the Wang Fuk Court fire, hoping the departed may rest in peace.

Li Kwok-wing said the requiem ritual had already been held discreetly this morning, and devotees may still visit the temple to offer incense.

Fisherfolk of the So, Tsui, Lee, Chung and Shek clans from Tai Po held a ritual at the Tin Hau Temple today. Yuen Chau Tsai fishing village representative Li Kwok-wing said Hakka clansmen pool funds every year to hold the Hailufeng Yu Lan Festival, offering sacrifices to lonely souls at sea. The Wang Fuk Court fire last year claimed at least 168 lives, and women in the clan began folding gold and silver paper and preparing clothes packages four days early to honour the spirits of their neighbourhood friends. Li Kwok-wing said the requiem ritual had already been held discreetly this morning, and devotees may still visit the temple to offer incense.

Additionally, at the Tin Hau Temple under the big tree in Yuen Long, with the support of the charitable group 'On Ling House', a three-day '2026 Breaking of Hell Universal Salvation Ritual' has been held from yesterday (the 25th) until tomorrow, specifically performing rites for the 168 deceased of Wang Fuk Court. Paper-craft master Mok Cheuk-ki crafted an 'extra-large Buddhist ship' bearing memorial tablets for the 168 Wang Fuk Court deceased; the tablets will be placed on the ship, with the 'Breaking of Hell' ceremony and sutra recitation performed, hoping the spirits may ascend to the Pure Land at an early date.

Recently an incident of a dog being bitten by another dog occurred in Yuen Long; the organisers also set up a pet area, establishing lotus memorial plaques for the Bichon Frise named Wai Wai that was killed by a large dog, another toy poodle, and other deceased stray animals.
